Oracle for the image fixtures in fixtures/images/. Written by hand from fixtures/ORIGEM.md (exiftool 13.60 + pillow-heif 1.8.1, columns "Gravado" and "Aparece") plus an independent ISO-BMFF/JPEG walk, and from the construction of each gen-* file. No engine code produced these numbers.
Per file: format = what the BYTES are (never the extension); storedWidth/storedHeight = pixels as stored (HEIC: ispe of the primary item, before irot); displayWidth/displayHeight = size on screen after applying the orientation ONCE (HEIC: the container irot/imir, never the Exif tag on top of it);
orientation = Exif Orientation tag 1-8 (1 when there is none); hasGps = the GPS IFD pointer (Exif tag 0x8825) is present, which is what no output may carry; gpsKind = real (coordinates), zeroed (0/1 rationals, heic-10), empty (empty refs and 0/0 rationals, heic-09) or none;
hasAlpha = the pixels carry real transparency; imageCount = top-level images in the file (heic-10 = 2, the primary is item 26); animated = more than one frame; expect = what the engine must do with the file: ok (decodes), empty (0 bytes), unsupported (not an image), truncated (cut short), decode (marker structure damaged, no browser decodes it).
heif (HEIC only): majorBrand/compatibleBrands = the ftyp box; primaryItemId = pitm; primaryType = item type of the primary (grid in all ten); ispe = [w,h] of the primary; irot = degrees ANTICLOCKWISE stored in the irot property of the primary (null when absent); imir = null (no fixture has one); exifItem = an Exif item exists; exifItemIds, topLevelImageItemIds, auxiliaryItemIds, thumbnailItemIds = ids, so a parser test can prove the engine ignores gain maps, depth maps and thumbnails; iccDisplayP3 = the primary carries a Display P3 ICC profile (heic-09 has no colr at all, so it is sRGB).
Exif PixelXDimension/PixelYDimension are NOT reliable (heic-01..08 say 4032x3024 whatever the real size): never compare against them.
Generated files (gen-*, built by scripts/fixtures/generate.ts, SHA-256 in fixtures/ORIGEM.md): the values follow from the construction of each file. A null size means no reader can trust one (corrupt) or there is no image (text, empty). frameCount (animated WebP) = ANMF frames; pixels = width x height when a file exists to sit above a limit.

notes: Exif PixelXDimension/PixelYDimension say 4032x3024 but the image is 3024x4032 portrait with irot=0 and Orientation 1: never use Exif dimensions. Also carries an XMP item (application/rdf+xml).
Exif PixelXDimension/PixelYDimension say 4032x3024 but the image is 3024x4032 portrait with irot=0 and Orientation 1: never use Exif dimensions. Also carries an XMP item (application/rdf+xml).
Exif PixelXDimension/PixelYDimension say 4032x3024 but the image is 3024x4032 portrait with irot=0 and Orientation 1: never use Exif dimensions. Also carries an XMP item (application/rdf+xml).

No Exif Orientation tag (null) and irot=0. Exif PixelXDimension/PixelYDimension say 4032x3024 but the image is 2566x3313 (portrait): never use Exif dimensions. 42 tiles (7x6 of 512) cover 3072x3584 > 2566x3313: the grid output size crops the tile canvas.

Double-rotation trap: primary grid is stored 4032x3024 with irot=270 (anticlockwise) = 90 clockwise; Exif Orientation is 6 as well. Orientation must be applied ONCE (container), never again from Exif. Wrong result is 4032x3024 (lying down) or upside-down. Correct: 3024x4032.
HDR gain map is auxiliary item 51 (2016x1512, irot 270) - must be ignored; thumbnail item 50 (320x240, irot 270) must be ignored.
Has a 320x240 thumbnail item (50) - must be ignored.
Auxiliary items: 52 HDR gain map (2016x1512), 54 depth (768x576, urn:mpeg:hevc:2015:auxid:2). Both hidden, must be ignored. GPS is real (the owners published it).

Exif PixelXDimension/PixelYDimension say 4032x3024 but the image is 1512x850 (author downscaled): never use Exif dimensions. The HDR gain map (aux item 10, 756x426) carries a clap (756x425) - only on the aux image, not the primary.

ORIGEM says this file has real GPS; it does not. The Exif has the GPS IFD pointer (tag 0x8825, tags 1-4) but LatRef/LonRef are empty strings and both rationals are 0/0: an empty placeholder. It still counts as "GPS tag present" (hasGps true), so it is a valid negative control, like heic-10.

Same double-rotation trap as heic-05 (irot=270 + Exif Orientation 6). No colr/ICC (treat as sRGB). meta box comes AFTER mdat, then a trailing non-standard box sefd. GPS DISCREPANCY: ORIGEM says real GPS; the file has the GPS IFD (tag 0x8825: tags 1-4) but LatRef/LonRef are empty strings and both rationals are 0/0 (empty placeholder). Treat like heic-10: tag present, no coordinates.

Two top-level grid items (26 = primary/left eye, 52 = right eye) in a ster group (grpl). Output must be ONE file from item 26 (pitm). libheif-js decode() returns both ([0].is_primary()=true, [1]=false). GPS IFD present on the primary Exif (item 54): LatRef N, LonRef E, all rationals 0/1, AltRef 0, Alt 0/1 -> zeroed (0,0); tag must still vanish. The right-eye Exif (item 55) has no GPS. Primary has no irot/imir. Items carry 3 uuid properties each (Apple spatial metadata).
APP1 carries an embedded Exif thumbnail JPEG with its own SOI/SOF: a naive search for FFC0 finds the thumbnail first. Read SOF from top-level segments only.
APP1 (39,264 bytes) comes BEFORE JFIF (APP0); ICC_PROFILE APP2 is sRGB IEC61966-2.1 (596 bytes).
APP1 carries an embedded Exif thumbnail JPEG with its own SOI/SOF: a naive search for FFC0 finds the thumbnail first. Read SOF from top-level segments only.
Orientation 3 = rotate 180: dimensions do NOT change (3264x2448 stored and displayed), so only a pixel comparison (not size) detects a missing/doubled rotation.
APP1 carries an embedded Exif thumbnail JPEG with its own SOI/SOF: a naive search for FFC0 finds the thumbnail first. Read SOF from top-level segments only.

jpg-01 reduced to 1200x1600 upright, stored turned 90 degrees counter-clockwise (1600x1200), so Orientation 6 (rotate 90 clockwise) shows it upright. The APP1 is the ORIGINAL one of jpg-01 with only the Orientation value changed from 1 to 6: GPS is kept.
The stale tags are left as they were (IFD0 ImageWidth/ImageLength and ExifIFD PixelXDimension/PixelYDimension say 3024x4032, the Exif thumbnail is the unrotated 189x252): never read size from them.
The browsers apply the Orientation by themselves; the stored pixels are what jpeg.ts withOrientation(bytes, 1) lets a test decode.

jpg-02 at 1600x1200 upright, stored turned 90 degrees clockwise (1200x1600), so Orientation 8 (rotate 90 counter-clockwise) shows it upright. ORIGINAL APP1 of jpg-02, only the Orientation changed from 1 to 8: GPS is kept.
Stale tags as in the Orientation 6 file (3264x2448 in the Exif, thumbnail 160x120 unrotated).

jpg-03 (upright) at 800x600 with an alpha fade: opaque in the middle (alpha 255), partly transparent around the middle of the edges, fully transparent (alpha 0) in the four corners. Colour type 6, chunks IHDR, IDAT..., IEND only.
Flattened on white the corners are white; flattened on black they would be black: that tells the conversions apart.

jpg-02 at 1600x1200 as lossy WebP in a VP8X container with the EXIF flag and an EXIF chunk after the image. The chunk holds the TIFF block of jpg-02 (real GPS, Orientation 1) without the "Exif\0\0" prefix, as the WebP spec says; readers must accept both.

VP8X (animation flag), ANIM, two ANMF frames of 320x240, 500 ms each. Frame 1 is a red field (#d9381e), frame 2 a blue field (#1e5ad9), each with a white band and a ring. WebP to JPG/PNG must output frame 1 (red) and say so. The jSquash WebP decoder throws on it: the browser decode is the only way.

jpg-03 with its Orientation 3 applied (turned 180 degrees) at 1600x1200, so the file is upright with no rotation property and no Exif. Encoded by @jsquash/avif in Node (single-thread build), quality 50, speed 8.

The AVIF side of the AVIF-or-HEIC sniffing case: major brand avif, mif1 among the compatible brands. Chromium decodes it; the WebKit 27.2 of Playwright on Windows does not (createImageBitmap rejects it), so a test that needs the pixels decodes it in Chromium only.

A 1600x1200 baseline JPEG of jpg-02 cut at 60% of its bytes: SOI, tables, SOF and the first rows of the scan are intact, there is no EOI. Chromium refuses to decode it; WebKit decodes the top part without an error. Both outcomes happen, so the engine must recognise the file by its structure (no EOI) and refuse it with the incomplete-file message.

A valid 800x600 JPEG of jpg-02 with its marker structure damaged: the length of the first DQT points into the scan data and the SOF height is 0. It starts with FF D8 FF and ends with FF D9, so a check of the first and last bytes accepts it. A marker walk throws (bad marker at 1520), and neither Chromium nor WebKit decodes it. The size is null because no reader can trust the SOF.

PNG bytes (jpg-02 at 640x480, opaque, RGBA colour type with all alpha 255) in a file called .jpg. The type comes from the bytes, so Compress image gives a .png back, Image to PDF embeds it as a PNG and the JPG tools treat it as a PNG.
Two lines of UTF-8 text in a file called .png. Not an image: the tools refuse it with the not-an-image message and the rest of the batch goes on.
0 bytes, called .jpg. Refused with the empty-file message.

4100 x 4100 = 16,810,000 px, 32,784 above the 16,777,216 px (4096 x 4096) canvas limit of Safari on iPhone, so it takes the no-canvas path. A gradient and flat colour blocks with no Exif: small (about 190 KB) and cheap to decode. The boundary itself (4096 x 4096, not "above") belongs in a unit test of the decision function, not in a file.
